title: Failover coordinator and rapid KV-drain reconciliation for customer-facing rollouts
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Summary:
We need an automated, tenant-aware failover coordinator that performs a rapid KV-cache drain and model-route reconciliation when canary quality degrades or silent regressions are detected across Hosted/Dedicated/Private planes. Recent incidents showed that model variant pinning + stale KV caches cause intermittent hallucinations and customer-visible regressions during cross-variant rollouts. This ticket implements: 1) a fast KV-drain + reconciliation mechanism that runs atomically with variant rollbacks, 2) an ops coordinator service (statemachine) to sequence traffic drains, model pin flips, and tenant notifications, and 3) incident playbook pages and customer communication templates for SRE/CS and field teams.
success_criteria: 1) Canaries that breach quality thresholds (see detection rules) automatically enter a containment flow within 90s. 2) KV-drain completes such that subsequent requests do not observe mixed KV state across model families. 3) Rollbacks finish with no more than 2x baseline tail-latency impact and no more than 0.5% additional error budget consumption for affected tenants. 4) Runbook actions and customer emails are templated and validated by Solutions and Legal.
background_and_rationale: Problem: When switching traffic between model variants (e.g., quantized fallback -> full-precision) we observed stale KV entries persisted in fronting caches and local slice caches, producing out-of-distribution context and amplification of regressions. Dedicated and Private deployments add complexity because KV cache invalidation paths vary (local cache, VPC-edge, redis-shared, and in-process caches). Approach: avoid broad cache purges which cause high tail latency; instead perform selective KV-drain + reconciliation tied to the rollout statemachine so impacted tenant slices are safely quiesced and traffic moved in a controlled, observable manner.
plan_of_work: 1) Detection rules (ENG/Telemetry): implement a canary quality monitor that computes per-tenant signal: perplexity shift, response-fluency regression, and syntactic error spike. 2) Failover coordinator service: state transitions (DETECT -> QUARANTINE -> KV-DRAIN -> PIN-ROLLBACK -> VALIDATE -> RELEASE). 3) KV-drain tool: implement selective TTL reduction + per-tenant key prefixed invalidations + graceful fallback to full-cache-eviction for catastrophic regressions. 4) Integrations: Console dashboard widgets, API hooks for Dedicated agents, and a Private deployment agent to run the drain locally. 5) Communications: templates for customer outreach (CS/AE), postmortem skeletons, and SLA adjustments if needed. 6) Tests: end-to-end staging runs, chaos tests that inject stale KV and verify reconciliation. 7) Docs & Runbook: Confluence runbook + Slack playbook command (/failover run ENG-492811).
detection_thresholds: - Canary failure if 3-minute rolling window shows >12% decrease in semantic-similarity vs baseline OR >8% increase in model hallucination markers AND acceptance tests fail for >20% of sampled prompts. - Automatic quarantine if threshold met for 2 consecutive windows.
kv_draining_strategy: Phase A: selective prefix invalidation for keys touched by the new model (uses model-keymap generated during compile-time). Phase B: soft-TTL shrink for remaining keys (90% TTL reduction) to allow in-flight friendly eviction. Phase C (fallback): full-eviction targeted at affected slices only. All phases execute with rate-limits to keep tail latency within SLOs.
rollout_and_fallback_sequence: 1) Detect breach -> mark affected tenant slice. 2) Pause canary expansion and route new requests for slice to quarantine workers. 3) Kick off KV-drain (Phase A). 4) Flip model pin on quarantine workers to last-known-good variant. 5) Run validation harness (synthetic + sampled production prompts). 6) If validation OK, resume traffic gradually; else escalate to human-in-loop rollback and open hotpatch channel.
communication_plan: - Initial internal alert to #sre-ops and #field-liaison with incident tag and affected-tenants list. - Customer template: succinct incident summary, expected timeline, mitigation steps (temporary pin to prior model), and contact for escalations. - Post-incident: technical postmortem and a customer-facing summary checked by Legal.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive KV eviction causes latency spikes and increased origin load. Mitigation: rate-limit drain, perform in slices, fallback to read-through mode for high-QPS tenants. Risk: Private deployments cannot accept remote KV invalidations. Mitigation: include an agent-based local drain tool that runs as part of the Private control-plane upgrade and requires customer opt-in with clear rollback path.
open_questions: - Do we want automated tenant opt-out for automated pin-rollbacks? (PM/Legal decision) - Should we persist a small shadow cache to accelerate rehydrate after drain?
implementation_notes: - Use existing kernel-selection hooks to tag keys written by a model variant. - KV keymap generation happens at compile-time and is stored in model-metadata. - Coordinator exposes a /v1/failover POST endpoint with authenticated JWT and a 'dry_run' flag. - Include circuit-breaker metrics (drain-rate, evict-errors, validation-failures).
testing_and_validation: - Staging job 'canary-kv-sanity' that injects synthetic stale KV entries and runs the full coordinator sequence. - Chaos test: killing 30% of quarantine workers mid-drain to ensure reconciliation idempotence. - Canary release across 5 internal tenants for observability prior to broad rollout.
rollback_checklist: 1) Stop new failover auto-runs. 2) Re-pin traffic to previous variant. 3) Rehydrate caches from snapshot if available or re-synthesize top-K prefixes for affected slices. 4) Communicate to customers and set support priority. 5) Open hotpatch PR and attach logs and validation diffs.
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Rao: Ticket created after postmortem for incident-489002. Initial proposal attached to Confluence. Assigned to Markus for execution.

2026-03-03 Markus Chen: Spiked an implementation of a selective prefix invalidator in the dev branch. Found inconsistent key-tagging for some older model artifacts — added a migration step to model-metadata generator.
2026-03-05 Aisha Patel (SRE): Added detection alert rule to staging (canary-quality-v2). Observed one false positive on high-latency tail; reduced sensitivity window from 5m to 3m.
2026-03-07 Priya Rao (PM): Reviewed customer communication draft. Legal requested removal of the phrase 'root cause' from customer-facing text; updated template.
2026-03-09 Markus Chen: Integrated Private-agent hook for local drains. Currently gated behind feature flag private-kv-drain. Need QA sign-off for on-prem agent packaging.
2026-03-11 QA: Running end-to-end staging run. Found an edge-case where drain rate-limiter blocks validation traffic; adjusting guardrails to exempt validation harness requests.
2026-03-12 Markus Chen: Dry-run successful across 3 internal tenants. Preparing PR for review. Next: schedule canary internal rollout and coordinate with SRE for next-week runbook rehearsal.
